title: Wait and watch

controls.label: Time (quarters after the fall in AD)

readouts.v: {gap<-0.05 ? "above the natural rate" : "at the natural rate"}

predict.q: AD has just fallen: the economy is in a recessionary gap, with output 4% below potential. With no policy, wages and prices fully adjust. Where does the economy end up?

options.s: Output stays 4% below potential for good
options.fb: Only if wages never fall. Here wages are flexible, so SRAS keeps shifting right while unemployment is above its natural rate.

options.s: Output back at potential, price level lower than before the fall in AD
options.fb: Wages fall, SRAS shifts right until output is back at potential; it meets the lower AD at a lower price level (about 97 against 110).

options.s: Output back at potential, price level back to where it started
options.fb: AD is still lower than at the start, so the price level ends lower: SRAS meets the lower AD on LRAS.

options.s: Output back at potential because LRAS shifts left to meet it
options.fb: LRAS is capacity, which a fall in spending does not destroy here. SRAS moves, not LRAS.

task: Move the time slider to 12 and watch nominal wages fall, SRAS shift right and output close the gap.

target.do: Move the time slider to 12 quarters, then press Check.

takeaway: Self-adjustment works through wages and SRAS; output returns to potential at a lower price level.
